questions.question:
In the year 1916, which of the following month had 5 Wednesdays?

I. June II. December
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The number of times a particular day occurs in a month depends on the total **number of days** in that month and the **day of the week** it starts on:

__
 
• A month with **30 days** will have 5 of a specific day if the month starts on that day or the day before it (i.e., the day must fall on the **1st** or **2nd** of the month).
 
• A month with **31 days** will have 5 of a specific day if the month starts on that day or up to two days before it (i.e., the day must fall on the **1st**, **2nd**, or **3rd** of the month).

**Calculation:**__

The year **1916** is divisible by 4, making it a **leap year**. Therefore, **February** has 29 days.

First, we determine the day of the week for **January 1, 1916**. Using the calendar calculation, January 1, 1916, was a **Saturday**.

**I. June 1916**

**June** always has **30 days**.

Total days from January 1 to **June 1** = 31 (Jan) + 29 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 30 (Apr) + 31 (May) = 152 days.

Odd days = 152 ÷ 7 = 21 weeks and **5 odd days**.

Day on **June 1** = Saturday + 5 days = **Thursday**.

Since June starts on a **Thursday**, the **Wednesdays** fall on the 7th, 14th, 21st, and 28th. There are only **4 Wednesdays** in June 1916.

**II. December 1916**

**December** always has **31 days**.

Total days from June 1 to **December 1** = 30 (Jun) + 31 (Jul) + 31 (Aug) + 30 (Sep) + 31 (Oct) + 30 (Nov) = 183 days.

Odd days = 183 ÷ 7 = 26 weeks and **1 odd day**.

Day on **December 1** = Thursday + 1 day = **Friday**.

Since December starts on a **Friday**, the **Wednesdays** fall on the 6th, 13th, 20th, and 27th. There are only **4 Wednesdays** in December 1916.

Therefore, neither June nor December had 5 Wednesdays in the year **1916**.

Therefore, the correct option is **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

We can use the day of the week formula: Day = (Date + Month Code + Year Code + Century Code + Leap Year Adjustment) mod 7.

For the year **1916**: Year = 16, Leap Year count = 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Century Code (1900s) = 0.

For **June 1** (Month Code = 4): (1 + 4 + 16 + 4 + 0) mod 7 = 25 mod 7 = 4 (**Thursday**).

For **December 1** (Month Code = 5): (1 + 5 + 16 + 4 + 0) mod 7 = 26 mod 7 = 5 (**Friday**).

A **30-day month** (June) needs to start on Tuesday or Wednesday to have 5 Wednesdays. A **31-day month** (December) needs to start on Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday to have 5 Wednesdays.

Since June started on **Thursday** and December started on **Friday**, neither month had **5 Wednesdays**.

Hence, the correct answer is **Neither I nor II**.

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 10 AM and 11 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 15 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Hour hand** covers 3600 in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360/12 = 300

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 30/60 = 0.50

**Minute hand** covers 3600 in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 360/60 = 60

**__Calculation:__**

The given time is between **10 AM** and **11 AM**. Let the time be **10:M**.

At **10:00 AM**, the hour hand is at 10 × 300 = 3000 and the minute hand is at 00.

In **M** minutes:

Position of the **hour hand** = 3000 + 0.5 × M

Position of the **minute hand** = 6 × M

Angle between hands = |(300 + 0.5M) − 6M| = |300 − 5.5M|

Given the angle is **15 degrees**:

**Case 1:**

300 − 5.5M = 15 ⇒ 5.5M = 285

M = 285 / 5.5 ≈ 51.81 minutes

**Case 2:**

300 − 5.5M = −15 ⇒ 5.5M = 315

M = 315 / 5.5 ≈ 57.27 minutes

The approximate time from **Case 1** is **10:52 AM** (since 51.81 ≈ 52).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M| over 2

Here, H = 10 and Angle = 15.

15 = |60 times 10 - 11 times M| over 2

30 = |600 − 11M|

600 − 11M = 30 ⇒ 11M = 570 ⇒ M = 51.818...

600 − 11M = −30 ⇒ 11M = 630 ⇒ M = 57.272...

The closest value to the options is 51.82, which is approximately 52 minutes.

Hence, the correct answer is **10:52**

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 3 PM and 4 PM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 110 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The angle between the **hour hand** and the **minute hand** of a clock can be calculated using the following relationship:

Angle (θ) = |30H − 5.5M|

Where:

__
 
• **H** is the hour (in this case, **3**).
 
• **M** is the minutes past the hour.

Alternatively, we can look at the relative speeds:

Speed of the **minute hand** = 6° per minute

Speed of the **hour hand** = 0.5° per minute

The relative speed between the two hands is 5.5° per minute.

**Calculation:__**

We are looking for the time between **3 PM** and **4 PM** when the angle is **110 degrees**.

Given **H = 3** and **θ = 110°**.

Case 1: The minute hand is behind the hour hand (not possible for 110° starting from 3 PM, as 3:00 is only 90°).

Case 2: The minute hand is ahead of the hour hand.

110 = 5.5M − 30(3)

110 = 5.5M − 90

110 + 90 = 5.5M

200 = 5.5M

M = 200 ÷ 5.5

M = 400 ÷ 11

M = 36.3636...

Rounding to the nearest minute, we get **M ≈ 36**.

Therefore, the time is approximately **3:36 PM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

At **3:00 PM**, the angle between the hands is 90°.

To reach an angle of **110°**, the minute hand must first cover the 90° to overlap the hour hand and then move 110° ahead of it.

Total relative distance to be covered = 90° + 110° = 200°

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 200 ÷ 5.5

Time = 36.36 minutes

The approximate time is **3:36 PM**.

Hence, the correct answer is **3:36**.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of M and S is 2 : 5. M is 9 years younger than S. What will be the ratio of M's age to S's age after 12 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Present age ratio of M and S = **2 : 5**

M is **9 years younger** than S.

**Calculation:**

Let the present ages of M and S be **2x** and **5x**.

Difference = 5x − 2x = 9

3x = 9

x = 3

Present ages:

 
• M = 2 × 3 = **6 years**
 
• S = 5 × 3 = **15 years**

**After 12 years:**

M = 6 + 12 = **18 years**

S = 15 + 12 = **27 years**

**Required ratio:**

18 : 27 = 2 : 3

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**
